title: The Book of Hosea Timeline
sub: Marry a Prostitute · I Will Heal Their Waywardness
desc: A prophet's own unfaithful marriage becomes a living parable of Israel's spiritual adultery, moving through harsh judgment-names and covenant lawsuits to some of the most emotionally raw pictures of God's fatherly love in all of Scripture.

eras.label: Era One · Hosea 1
eras.name: Marry a Prostitute — Children Named as Living Warnings
eras.dates: Hosea's own marriage becomes a walking parable of Israel's unfaithfulness, with each of his children's names a coded message of coming judgment

events.title: Go, Marry a Prostitute — Jezreel, No Pity, Not My People
events.detail: Hosea is commanded to marry Gomer, an unfaithful woman, as a living illustration of Israel's spiritual adultery, then to name their three children Jezreel (coming judgment), No Pity, and Not My People, each name announcing the nation's broken relationship with God.

verses.text: “Name him ‘Not My People’ (Lo-Ammi) because you are not my people, and I am not your God.”

eras.label: Era Two · Hosea 2
eras.name: Children of the Living God — I Will Betroth You to Me Forever
eras.dates: The harsh judgment-names are reversed into promise, moving through a courtroom scene against unfaithful Israel into one of the tenderest restoration passages in the prophets. (The Hebrew text's chapter division falls two verses earlier than most English translations, marked inline in the NET text itself as “(2:1)”.)

events.title: You Are Children of the Living God — a Case Against an Unfaithful Wife
events.detail: Before the chapter turns to judgment, the harsh names of chapter 1 are reversed — the people will again be called 'My People' and 'Pity' — though a legal case against Israel's spiritual adultery follows, stripping away the false lovers she credited for her blessings.

verses.text: “Then you will call your brother, ‘My People’ (Ammi)! You will call your sister, ‘Pity’ (Ruhamah)!” (Numbered 1:10 in most English translations.)

events.title: I Will Allure Her Into the Wilderness — I Will Betroth You to Me Forever
events.detail: Judgment gives way to courtship: the LORD promises to lead Israel back into the wilderness to speak tenderly to her, remove the very names of the Baal idols from her lips, and commit himself to her forever in righteousness and steadfast love, closing with a promise to plant her again as his own.

verses.text: “In that day I will answer,” declares the LORD [Yahweh]. “I will answer the sky, and the sky will answer the ground.” (Numbered 2:21 in most English translations.)

eras.label: Era Three · Hosea 3
eras.name: Buy Her Back — They Will Seek the LORD Their God
eras.dates: Hosea is commanded to redeem Gomer a second time, buying back an unfaithful wife as a picture of Israel's eventual return

events.title: Go, Show Love to Your Wife Again — I Paid Silver and Barley to Purchase Her
events.detail: Hosea buys Gomer back for the price of a slave, requiring a period of separation before restoration, mirroring Israel's coming exile without king or sacrifice before its future return to seek the LORD and the Davidic king.

verses.text: “Afterward, the Israelites will turn and seek the LORD [Yahweh] their God [Elohim] and their Davidic king.”

eras.label: Era Four · Hosea 4
eras.name: No Knowledge of God in the Land — a Covenant Lawsuit
eras.dates: The personal marriage-parable gives way to a direct legal indictment of the whole nation, with priests singled out for special blame

events.title: My People Are Destroyed for Lack of Knowledge
events.detail: The LORD brings a covenant lawsuit against Israel for its lack of faithfulness and knowledge of God, directing particular blame at priests who fed on the people's sin offerings rather than teaching them the law.

verses.text: “My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge… because you have forgotten the law of your God [Elohim], I also will forget your children.”

eras.label: Era Five · Hosea 5
eras.name: I Will Be Like a Lion — Ephraim Turns to Assyria in Vain
eras.dates: Judgment falls on both Israel's princes and its priests, with Ephraim's desperate alliance with Assyria proving powerless to heal its real wound

events.title: I Will Be Like a Lion to Ephraim — Assyria Cannot Heal Your Wound
events.detail: Judah and Israel alike are indicted for idolatry, and when Ephraim turns to Assyria's great king for help against its sickness, the appeal fails — only the LORD, likened here to a lion and a moth, can address the real problem.

verses.text: “Ephraim turned to Assyria and begged its great king for help. But he will not be able to heal you… I will be like a lion to Ephraim.”

eras.label: Era Six · Hosea 6
eras.name: I Delight in Faithfulness, Not Sacrifice
eras.dates: A call to return to the LORD is met with one of the most quoted verses in the prophetic corpus about the priority of the heart over ritual

events.title: Come, Let's Return to the LORD — He Will Restore Us
events.detail: A call to genuine return expresses confidence that the LORD who tore the nation will also heal it, coming to their rescue as certainly as the dawn or the spring rain.

verses.text: “Come on! Let's return to the LORD [Yahweh]. He himself has torn us to pieces, but he will heal us!”

events.title: I Delight in Faithfulness, Not Sacrifice
events.detail: Israel's loyalty is dismissed as fleeting as the morning mist, and the LORD declares he wants genuine faithfulness and knowledge of God rather than empty ritual — the very verse Jesus later quotes twice against the Pharisees.

verses.text: “I delight in faithfulness, not simply in sacrifice; I delight in acknowledging God [Elohim], not simply in whole burnt offerings.”

eras.label: Era Seven · Hosea 7
eras.name: Like a Smoldering Oven — a Dove Easily Deceived
eras.dates: Court intrigue and foreign entanglements are compared to a baker's oven left unwatched, flaring up when least expected

events.title: Like a Dove, Easily Deceived — Calling to Egypt, Turning to Assyria
events.detail: Israel's leaders scheme against one another like a burning oven ready to flare up, while the nation as a whole flits between Egypt and Assyria for protection like a foolish, easily-deceived dove, never once calling on the LORD.

verses.text: “Ephraim has been like a dove, easily deceived and lacking discernment. They called to Egypt for help; they turned to Assyria for protection.”

eras.label: Era Eight · Hosea 8
eras.name: Sow the Wind, Reap the Whirlwind
eras.dates: Unauthorized kings, homemade idols, and empty sacrifices are summed up in one of the Bible's most quoted proverbs of consequence

events.title: They Sow the Wind, and So They Will Reap the Whirlwind
events.detail: Israel enthroned kings and appointed princes without the LORD's consent, made idols with their own silver and gold, and now faces the natural harvest of that unauthorized independence.

verses.text: “They sow the wind, and so they will reap the whirlwind! The stalk does not have any standing grain; it will not produce any flour.”

eras.label: Era Nine · Hosea 9
eras.name: Do Not Rejoice — Ephraim Will Return to Egypt
eras.dates: A festival celebration is interrupted with news that exile, not continued blessing, is what's actually coming

events.title: Ephraim Will Return to Egypt — Give Them Wombs That Miscarry
events.detail: Rather than continued festival joy, Israel faces exile back toward Egypt and Assyria, with a shocking prayer that childlessness itself would be better than raising children only to lose them to coming judgment.

verses.text: “My God will reject them, for they have not obeyed him; so they will be fugitives among the nations.”

eras.label: Era Ten · Hosea 10
eras.name: Sow Righteousness, Reap Unfailing Love
eras.dates: A fertile vine turned to idolatry is called back to genuine reform, using farming imagery to contrast wickedness harvested with righteousness that could still be sown

events.title: Sow Righteousness for Yourselves, Reap Unfailing Love
events.detail: Israel, a once-fruitful vine that multiplied altars to Baal as it prospered, is urged to break up its unplowed ground and seek the LORD, since it has plowed wickedness and reaped injustice instead.

verses.text: “Sow righteousness for yourselves, reap unfailing love. Break up the unplowed ground for yourselves, for it is time to seek the LORD [Yahweh].”

eras.label: Era Eleven · Hosea 11
eras.name: Out of Egypt I Called My Son — How Can I Give You Up?
eras.dates: God's fatherly love for Israel since infancy collides with his righteous anger, producing one of the most emotionally raw passages in the Old Testament. (The Hebrew text's chapter division falls one verse earlier than most English translations, marked inline in the NET text itself as “(12:1)”.)

events.title: Out of Egypt I Called My Son — I Led Them With Cords of Love
events.detail: God recalls loving Israel like a father loves a young son, teaching him to walk and healing him, even as that same son kept running further away toward the Baals — a passage Matthew later applies to Jesus's own return from Egypt.

verses.text: “When Israel was a young man, I loved him like a son, and I summoned my son out of Egypt.”

events.title: How Can I Give You Up, O Ephraim? — I Am God, Not Man
events.detail: Poised to destroy Israel like Admah and Zeboyim, God's compassion overrules his anger in one of Scripture's most vivid pictures of internal divine conflict, choosing restraint precisely because he is God and not a vengeful man.

verses.text: “How can I give you up, O Ephraim?… I have had a change of heart… I am God [El], and not man—I will not come in wrath!”

eras.label: Era Twelve · Hosea 12
eras.name: Jacob Struggled With God — A Covenant Lawsuit Against Judah
eras.dates: Israel's own ancestor Jacob becomes a case study in both cunning and genuine encounter with God, indicting the nation's present dishonest dealings

events.title: In the Womb He Attacked His Brother — Jacob Struggled With God
events.detail: A covenant lawsuit against Judah recalls Jacob's own struggle with an angel at Bethel, tying the nation's present dishonest dealings back to the same grasping character its ancestor eventually had to surrender. (The Hebrew text's chapter division falls one verse earlier than most English translations, marked inline in the NET text itself as “(12:1)”.)

verses.text: “Ephraim has surrounded me with lies; the house of Israel has surrounded me with deceit. But Judah still roams about with God.” (Numbered 11:12 in most English translations.)

events.title: Ephraim Boasts of Wealth — by a Prophet Israel Was Preserved
events.detail: Dishonest business practices and self-satisfied boasting about wealth are contrasted with the LORD's own history of using prophets, from Moses onward, to bring Israel out of Egypt and preserve its life.

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] brought Israel out of Egypt by a prophet, and due to a prophet Israel was preserved alive.” (Numbered 12:13 in most English translations.)

eras.label: Era Thirteen · Hosea 13
eras.name: I Am the LORD Your God — O Death, Where Are Your Plagues?
eras.dates: A final indictment of Ephraim's idolatry builds to a defiant rhetorical challenge to death itself, later echoed by Paul in his own resurrection argument. (The Hebrew text's chapter division falls one verse earlier than most English translations, marked inline in the NET text itself as “(14:1)”.)

events.title: I Am the LORD Your God From the Land of Egypt — Calf Kissers
events.detail: Israel's idol-making, mockingly called kissing calf idols, is set against the LORD's own exclusive claim as the nation's only deliverer since Egypt, before he turns to lion-and-leopard imagery of coming judgment.

verses.text: “I am the LORD [Yahweh] your God [Elohim] from the land of Egypt, and gods besides me you must not know, and a deliverer there is none except me.”

events.title: O Death, Where Are Your Plagues? — O Sheol, Where Is Your Destruction?
events.detail: Israel's kings, granted in anger and taken away in wrath, could not save the nation from a judgment described as inescapable as death itself — though the rhetorical challenge to death's plagues is later echoed triumphantly by Paul in 1 Corinthians 15.

verses.text: “Will I deliver them from the power of Sheol? No, I will not! Will I redeem them from death? No, I will not! O Death, bring on your plagues! O Sheol, bring on your destruction!”

eras.label: Era Fourteen · Hosea 14
eras.name: Return, O Israel — I Will Heal Their Waywardness
eras.dates: The book's final call to repentance is met not with more judgment but with an outpouring of tender restoration imagery, closing with a direct appeal to the reader's own discernment

events.title: Samaria Will Be Held Guilty
events.detail: A final, stark statement of Samaria's guilt for rebelling against its God closes the previous section before the book pivots into its closing call to return. (Numbered 13:16 in most English translations.)

verses.text: “Samaria will be held guilty because she rebelled against her God [Elohim].”

events.title: Return, O Israel — I Will Heal Their Waywardness and Love Them Freely
events.detail: The book closes with a call to return and a prayer of genuine repentance, answered with one of the tenderest promises in the prophets — healing, freely given love, and flourishing like a garden — before a final appeal for the wise to discern the LORD's ways.

verses.text: “I will heal their waywardness and love them freely, for my anger will turn away from them.”
“Who is wise? Let him discern these things! Who is discerning? Let him understand them! For the ways of the LORD [Yahweh] are right.”
